transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because I've been having these... eating episodes. And afterward, I just feel so gross and disappointed in myself. Like, I should really have more control. I mean, I clean up messes for a living—I'm a janitor over at the community college. Which is kind of funny because I actually took some classes there a few years ago. Mostly art history, which was super interesting but, you know, completely useless for finding a real job. My professor was this older guy who always wore tweed jackets, even when it was like ninety degrees out, and he would always bring his golden retriever to class... wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the eating. It's just... after it happens, I feel so bad that I end up writing really awful things about myself in my journal. Just really mean stuff.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives or diuretics to try to control your weight or get rid of the calories?

No, I don't do anything like that. I really hate throwing up. Actually, cleaning up after people who get sick is definitely the worst part of my job. Just last week, someone threw up in the second-floor women's restroom right near the biology labs, and I had to use this special industrial powder we keep in the supply closet. It's supposed to neutralize the odor and it smells like fake cherries, but honestly, it just makes the whole hallway smell like cherry vomit, which is almost worse. My supervisor, Brenda, she insists on buying the cheapest brand of it because she says the college is cutting our maintenance budget again. Brenda is always complaining about the budget, and she even tried to take away our good mop heads... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the laxatives and stuff. No, I don't do any of that. I just sit there and feel awful about myself.
Do you find that worries about your weight or body shape strongly influence how or when you eat?

Um, honestly, not really? I mean, I don't think so. I definitely feel bad about myself, but I wouldn't say I'm constantly obsessing over my weight or my shape or anything. Like, I wear these really baggy coveralls for work anyway, which are basically one-size-fits-nobody. They're this awful shade of navy blue that fades in the wash, and the zipper always gets stuck right around the middle. I actually had to ask my mom to sew a new zipper into mine because the college refused to issue me a new pair. My mom is really good at sewing, she makes these beautiful quilts out of old t-shirts. She made one for my cousin's baby shower last month, with all these vintage band tees... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Body shape. Yeah, I don't really think about it that much before I eat. It's just the eating itself that's the problem.
Can you describe what happens during one of these eating episodes? How much do you typically eat in one sitting?

Um, well, it usually happens on some nights after my cleaning shift. I'll be so tired, so I stop at the convenience store just meaning to grab a normal dinner, you know? But then... I end up getting a big bowl of ramen, and then several rice balls, and some fried chicken, and a bunch of sweets. And I just eat all of it in my room within like an hour or two. It's so much food. The convenience store near my apartment is actually really nice, though. It's one of those ones that's open 24/7, and the guy who works the night shift, I think his name is Marcus, he always plays this really obscure jazz music over the speakers. He told me once he plays the saxophone in a local band that performs on Thursdays at this little dive bar downtown. I've never been because I'm usually working, but I really like jazz. My grandpa used to listen to it all the time on this old record player he kept in his garage... wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the eating. Yeah, it's just a huge amount of food all at once, way more than I ever plan to eat.
During these eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual?

Yeah, I do. I eat really, really fast during those times. Like, I'll just be standing at the kitchen counter, or sometimes I'm sitting on my bed with my sketchbook still open, and I'm just shoving it in. I barely even taste anything, honestly, I'm just trying to get it all down before I can think too much about what I'm doing. Speaking of my sketchbook, I've been trying to learn how to draw hands lately, and they are so incredibly difficult. I bought this special set of charcoal pencils from the art supply store near campus—the one with the creaky wooden floors? The owner there, this older guy with a really impressive handlebar mustache, he told me that hands are the hardest thing for any artist to master. He said even the Renaissance masters struggled with them. He actually showed me this book of Da Vinci's sketches, and it was amazing to see all the little erasure marks and adjustments he made. It made me feel a lot better about my own messy drawings, honestly. I usually use a kneaded eraser, the kind that looks like gray putty, because it doesn't leave those annoying little crumbs everywhere. I hate sweeping up eraser crumbs, probably because I spend all day sweeping up dirt at work... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, eating fast. Yeah, I eat super quickly when it happens. Almost like I'm in a race or something.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you eat once you start?

Yeah, it really does. It's like... once I start, it feels like I just keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically. And even while I’m thinking in my head, like, 'Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,' I just... well, speaking of sketches, I was actually trying to finish this one drawing of the old library building on campus yesterday. The architecture there is so gorgeous, all that heavy gothic stonework. There's this one gargoyle right above the main entrance that looks exactly like my old landlord's pug, Barnaby. Barnaby used to wheeze so loud every time he walked up the stairs, poor little guy. He had this bright red harness with all these fake rhinestones glued to it because my landlord's wife was obsessed with bedazzling things. She even bedazzled her steering wheel, which honestly seems super dangerous if the airbag ever goes off, right? Like, just a face full of plastic diamonds... wait, I'm doing it again, sorry. Um, control. Right. Yeah, even when I'm telling myself to stop, I don’t actually stop until the food is completely gone, or I just feel way too uncomfortable to keep going.
Do you feel a lot of distress or emotional discomfort specifically about these eating episodes themselves, not just the aftermath?

Yeah, definitely. That's honestly the main reason I came in to see you. Because right after it happens, I just feel so gross and so incredibly disappointed in myself. It's like I should have more control, you know? And then I end up just sitting there and writing these really awful, mean things about myself in my journal. My journal is actually this really pretty leather-bound one I found at a thrift store last year. It has these little embossed leaves all over the cover, and the paper inside is that thick, slightly yellow kind that makes you feel like you're writing in some ancient tome. The thrift store where I got it is run by this sweet older lady who always smells like lavender and mothballs. She has this massive collection of vintage teacups in the window display, and she told me once that she's been collecting them since she was a little girl in England. She actually gave me a free teacup once just because I helped her reach a box on a high shelf. It has tiny blue cornflowers painted on it... wait, sorry, I'm rambling again. But yeah, the distress is really bad. I just feel terrible about myself after I eat like that.
Do these eating episodes usually happen during the night, or do they also occur at other times of the day?

Well, it's usually at night. Like, on some nights after my cleaning shift is over, I'll stop at the convenience store on the way back to my apartment. I usually just mean to grab, like, a normal dinner, but I end up getting a big bowl of ramen, several of those little rice balls, some fried chicken, and a bunch of sweets. And then I'll just eat it all in my room within an hour or two. The convenience store I go to is the one right on the corner of 4th and Elm, the one with the flickering neon sign? They have this really sweet cashier who always works the night shift. He has this massive collection of enamel pins on his lanyard—like, probably twenty of them. One of them is this really cute little frog wearing a mushroom hat, and another one is a slice of pizza with sunglasses. I asked him about them once, and he said he trades them online with people all over the world. He even got one from a guy in Australia that looks like a tiny jar of Vegemite. Have you ever tried Vegemite? I heard it's super salty and kind of weird-tasting, but people over there just love it on toast with butter. I usually prefer just regular strawberry jam on my toast, maybe some peanut butter if I'm feeling fancy... oh, wait, sorry. You asked about when it happens. Yeah, mostly at night after work, when I get all that food and eat it so fast.
Do these eating episodes ever happen at times other than in the evening, like during the day or early afternoon?

Um, let me think. No, not really during the day. It's pretty much just a night thing for me. During the day I'm usually too busy anyway, or I'm sleeping since my shifts can be weird. Like, yesterday I spent almost the whole afternoon trying to fix this broken vacuum cleaner in the supply closet on the third floor. The belt had completely snapped, and it was making this horrendous screeching noise, like a banshee or something. Have you ever heard a banshee? I mean, obviously not a real one, but like in those old horror movies? I love old horror movies. The black and white ones, specifically. There's just something so atmospheric about the lighting they used back then, all those harsh shadows. I actually watched 'Nosferatu' last weekend on this tiny little portable DVD player I found at a garage sale. The screen is only like five inches wide, and the battery barely holds a charge, but it feels so nostalgic. The guy running the garage sale had all these boxes of old VHS tapes too, mostly recorded off the TV in the 90s. You could still see the commercials for, like, old fast food toys and stuff... wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right. Daytime. No, it doesn't really happen during the day, just at night.
